defects: Stray wireframe outline squares stay visible at lower-left after the wordmark resolves (pairs row 3, right frame): leftover build scaffolding
The tiled 'S' in OFFSET reads as '$' because the vertical stroke runs through the bowl, which hurts legibility of the hero word
The wordmark build shows half-resolved tiles with dark navy/black fills and outline placeholders. That reads as unfinished, not designed
The shot structure fails pace (longest shot 7.9s, median 3.2s). Per-second change falls to 1.5–2.6 around 9–11s, so the end card sits almost static
The pattern-to-pattern transitions look procedural: tiles flip with a uniform stagger and a similar arc each time, with no visible overshoot, settle or per-tile weight
Lighting is flat and even across the tile wall, and the bevels and grout give little sense of material. Crop edges are clean but slightly soft, with no specular or glaze detail on the ceramic
End-card lower-third text is small and low-contrast (yellow on mid-blue) next to the hero lockup
gaps: Choreography: one transition device (mass tile rotation) is repeated across all four beats with the same timing curve. Top work would vary scale, camera, direction and rhythm, and give the flips physical weight (anticipation, overshoot, staggered settle with offsets that land on the beat). It would also cut the 7.9s hold into tighter beats

Finish and materiality: the azulejo concept calls for real ceramic (glaze, specular roll-off, irregular grout, subtle surface variation), but the render is clean flat CG. The build state of the wordmark (placeholder outlines, stray squares) needs to be designed, not left showing

Sound: the spectrogram shows a dense, steady broadband percussive grid with one lift at ~7.5s and little dynamic arc. The hits look regular, not keyed to individual tile flips, and the track lacks foley-grade ceramic clicks and placement sounds. There is also no clear swell or silence to sell the logo resolve
